problem.concept: They face shortcomings to collect and annotate hateful speech due to the incompleteness and noisiness of OSN text and the subjectivity of hate speech.
These limitations are often aided with constraints that oversimplify the problem, such as considering only tweets containing hate-related words.

method.concept: We develop and employ a robust methodology to collect and annotate hateful users which does not depend directly on lexicon and where the users are annotated given their entire profile.
semi-supervised learning over a graph

contribution.concept: We develop and employ a robust methodology to collect and annotate hateful users which does not depend directly on lexicon and where the users are annotated given their entire profile.
This results in a sample of Twitter's retweet graph containing $100,386$ users, out of which $4,972$ were annotated.
We show that hateful users differ from normal ones in terms of their activity patterns, word usage and as well as network structure.
We obtain similar results comparing the neighbors of hateful vs. neighbors of normal users and also suspended users vs. active users, increasing the robustness of our analysis.

We observe that hateful users are densely connected, and thus formulate the hate speech detection problem as a task of semi-supervised learning over a graph, exploiting the network of connections on Twitter.

We find that a node embedding algorithm, which exploits the graph structure, outperforms content-based approaches for the detection of both hateful ($95\%$ AUC vs $88\%$ AUC) and suspended users ($93\%$ AUC vs $88\%$ AUC).

task.concept: learn emoji-based representations of resource-poor languages

method.concept: CESNA
CESNA model consists of twin Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory Recurrent Neural Networks (Bi-LSTM RNN) with shared parameters joined by a contrastive loss function based on a similarity metric.

contribution.concept: CESNA

Experiments on large-scale Twitter datasets of resource-rich languages - English and Spanish and resource-poor languages - Hindi and Telugu reveal that CESNA outperforms the state-of-the-art emoji prediction approaches based on distributional semantics, semantic rules, lexicon lists and deep neural network representations without shared parameters.

task.concept: translating between multiple source and target languages.

method.concept: task-specific attention models

Our approach seeks to retain as much of the parameter sharing generalization of NMT models as possible, while still allowing for language-specific specialization of the attention model to a particular language-pair or task.

contribution.concept: We propose task-specific attention models, a simple but effective technique for improving the quality of sequence-to-sequence neural multilingual translation.

Our experiments on four languages of the Europarl corpus show that using a target-specific model of attention provides consistent gains in translation quality for all possible translation directions, compared to a model in which all parameters are shared.

four languages of the Europarl corpus: We observe improved translation quality even in the (extreme) low-resource zero-shot translation directions for which the model never saw explicitly paired parallel data.

problem.concept: social media: facilitates anti-social behaviors including online harassment, cyberbullying, and hate speech.

task.concept: We study the distinctive characteristics of hate instigators and targets in terms of their profile self-presentation, activities, and online visibility.

method.concept: multi-step classification process
personality analysis of hate instigators and targets

contribution.concept: In this paper, we present the first comparative study of hate speech instigators and target users on Twitter.
Through a multi-step classification process, we curate a comprehensive hate speech dataset capturing various types of hate.
We find that hate instigators target more popular and high profile Twitter users, and that participating in hate speech can result in greater online visibility.
We conduct a personality analysis of hate instigators and targets and show that both groups have eccentric personality facets that differ from the general Twitter population.

method.concept: local word embeddings (in particular GloVe vectors), i.e., embeddings trained from the single document under consideration.

contribution.concept: This work presents a novel unsupervised method for keyphrase extraction, whose main innovation is the use of local word embeddings (in particular GloVe vectors), i.e., embeddings trained from the single document under consideration.

Empirical results offer evidence that indeed local representations lead to better keyphrase extraction results compared to both embeddings trained on very large third corpora or larger corpora consisting of several documents of the same scientific field and to other state-of-the-art unsupervised keyphrase extraction methods.

problem.concept: AbstractMost approaches to emotion analysis in fictional texts focus on detecting the emotion expressed in text. We argue that this is a simplification which leads to an overgeneralized interpretation of the results, as it does not take into account who experiences an emotion and why.

Emotions play a crucial role in the interaction between characters and the events they are involved in. Until today, no specific corpora that capture such an interaction were available for literature.

task.concept: Annotation of a Literature Corpus with Semantic Roles of Emotions
automatic prediction of these relational structures

method.concept: manually annotated for spans which correspond to emotion trigger phrases and entities/events in the roles of experiencers, targets, and causes of the emotion.
statistical models: joint modeling of emotions with its roles in all subtasks.

contribution.concept: We aim at filling this gap and present a publicly available corpus based on Project Gutenberg, REMAN (Relational EMotion ANnotation), manually annotated for spans which correspond to emotion trigger phrases and entities/events in the roles of experiencers, targets, and causes of the emotion.

We provide baseline results for the automatic prediction of these relational structures and show that emotion lexicons are not able to encompass the high variability of emotion expressions and demonstrate that statistical models benefit from joint modeling of emotions with its roles in all subtasks.

contribution.concept: Begin with an insightful adversarial attack on VSE embeddings, we show the limitation of current frameworks and image-text datasets (e.g., MS-COCO) both quantitatively and qualitatively.
We alleviate this problem by augmenting the MS-COCO image captioning datasets with textual contrastive adversarial samples.
These samples are synthesized using linguistic rules and the WordNet knowledge base. The construction procedure is both syntax- and semantics-aware.

augmenting the MS-COCO image captioning datasets with textual contrastive adversarial samples: This simple but powerful technique brings a noticeable improvement over the baselines on a diverse set of downstream tasks, in addition to defending known-type adversarial attacks.

task.concept: predicting English notional anaphora in context

method.concept: ensemble approach

contribution.concept: Using the OntoNotes corpus, this paper takes an ensemble approach to predicting English notional anaphora in context on the basis of the largest empirical data to date.

Using the OntoNotes corpus: In addition to state of the art prediction accuracy, the results suggest that theoretical approaches positing a plural construal at the antecedent’s utterance are insufficient, and that circumstances at the anaphor’s utterance location, as well as global factors such as genre, have a strong effect on the choice of referring expression.

method.concept: initialize an embedding-learning model with distributional vectors.

contribution.concept: In this paper, we initialize an embedding-learning model with distributional vectors.

In this paper, we initialize an embedding-learning model with distributional vectors. Evaluation on word similarity shows that this initialization significantly increases the quality of embeddings for rare words.

While Facebook, Twitter, Google have attempted to take several steps to tackle the hateful content, they have mostly been unsuccessful.
Lack of carefully curated data largely inhibits such understanding.

task.concept: characterizing the linguistic structure of counterspeech
automatically detect counterspeech in YouTube videos
detect different types of counterspeech in a comment

method.concept: measurement study
psycholinguistic analysis
machine learning models
multilabel models

contribution.concept: In this paper, we create and release the first ever dataset for counterspeech using comments from YouTube. The data contains 13,924 manually annotated comments where the labels indicate whether a comment is a counterspeech or not.

This analysis results in various interesting insights such as: the counterspeech comments receive much more likes as compared to the non-counterspeech comments, for certain communities majority of the non-counterspeech comments tend to be hate speech, the different types of counterspeech are not all equally effective and the language choice of users posting counterspeech is largely different from those posting non-counterspeech as revealed by a detailed psycholinguistic analysis.
Finally, we build a set of machine learning models that are able to automatically detect counterspeech in YouTube videos with an F1-score of 0.71.
We also build multilabel models that can detect different types of counterspeech in a comment with an F1-score of 0.60.

problem.concept: The task is challenging due to the large search space and spuriousness of logical forms.

method.concept: neural parser-ranker system

The parser generates candidate tree-structured logical forms from utterances using clues of denotations. These candidates are then ranked based on two criterion: their likelihood of executing to the correct denotation, and their agreement with the utterance semantics.
scheduled training procedure to balance the contribution of the two objectives.
neurally encoded lexicon to inject prior domain knowledge to the model.

contribution.concept: In this paper we introduce a neural parser-ranker system for weakly-supervised semantic parsing.
We present a scheduled training procedure to balance the contribution of the two objectives.
Furthermore, we propose to use a neurally encoded lexicon to inject prior domain knowledge to the model.
Experiments on three Freebase datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our semantic parser, achieving results within the state-of-the-art range.

task.concept: evaluating the grammaticality of the predictions of a language model.

method.concept: We automatically construct a large number of minimally different pairs of English sentences, each consisting of a grammatical and an ungrammatical sentence. The sentence pairs represent different variations of structure-sensitive phenomena: subject-verb agreement, reflexive anaphora and negative polarity items.
LSTM language model
Multi-task training with a syntactic objective (CCG supertagging)

contribution.concept: We present a dataset for evaluating the grammaticality of the predictions of a language model.

We automatically construct a large number of minimally different pairs of English sentences, each consisting of a grammatical and an ungrammatical sentence. The sentence pairs represent different variations of structure-sensitive phenomena: subject-verb agreement, reflexive anaphora and negative polarity items.
In an experiment using this data set, an LSTM language model performed poorly on many of the constructions.

Multi-task training with a syntactic objective (CCG supertagging) improved the LSTM's accuracy, but a large gap remained between its performance and the accuracy of human participants recruited online.
This suggests that there is considerable room for improvement over LSTMs in capturing syntax in a language model.
